named_events.loss_description: PCS' initial estimate of Hurricane Ida was $26bn. This has now moved out to approximately $27.5bn. Modelling firms' and financial analysts estimates range from $17bn to excess of USD 40bn. Most recently (Jan 2022) Munich Re has estimated Ida at $36bn.

Four individual events topped the $20bn threshold for economic loss for only the second time ever being Hurricane Ida, Flooding in Europe (Bernd), Summer flooding in China and the Polar Vortex in North America in February 2021

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a net strengthening of prior year reserves of GBP 3.217 million, representing 2.05% of its opening gross claims outstanding. This movement is derived from the gross claims development table, showing mixed development across older underwriting years, with a net adverse impact. While the syndicate does not anticipate adverse development in its Casualty reserves, other lines or older years contributed to the overall strengthening.
raw_causal_phrases: We continue to believe that the industry will see a deterioration of casualty results from previous accident years.
We do not currently anticipate adverse development in our Casualty reserves and this has again been ratified by independent actuarial opinion.
Adjustments to the amounts of claims provisions established in prior years are reflected in the financial statements for the period in which the adjustments are made.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development calculated from the gross claims development table as no explicit gross prior year movement figure was provided. The Managing Agent's report mentions a net profit of GBP 3.970m on the 2019 closed year of account, which is a net release, but the gross claims development table indicates a gross strengthening for the 2019 YOA.
